thesis_statement: Amazon combines the reaccelerating AWS franchise (fastest growth in 18 quarters at a $169B annualized run rate) with high-margin advertising and scaled retail logistics; 43% operating income growth shows the margin flywheel, while AI capex temporarily drives trailing free cash flow negative.

base.summary: AWS sustains roughly 30% growth, consolidated operating margin holds, and capex growth plateaus in 2027 allowing free cash flow to recover.
drivers: retail logistics scale and delivery-speed gains

bull.summary: AI demand keeps AWS accelerating above 40% with a Trainium cost advantage, and the Anthropic/OpenAI multi-gigawatt commitments anchor a decade of cloud growth.
drivers: Trainium adoption by leading AI labs

bear.summary: AI capex overrun persists, free cash flow stays negative into 2027, retail margin stalls and hyperscaler competition compresses AWS pricing.

key_risks: Free cash flow is negative (TTM -$7.6B) on a $66.1B YoY capex increase; the thesis depends on that capex converting into revenue.

Q2 net income of $62.6B includes $53.4B of pre-tax other income, primarily Anthropic investment marks; diluted EPS of $5.75 is not an operating run rate. Operating income of $27.5B is the real signal.
Aggregator fundamentals lag at Q1 2026 (period_end 2026-03-31, data_quality partial) - the same feed lag already recorded for ETN and GS; this thesis uses the official Q2 release instead.

fundamental: AWS segment year-over-year growth decelerates below 25% for two consecutive quarters.
Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow remains negative beyond mid-2027 without a credible recovery path.
North America segment operating margin falls below 4% for two consecutive quarters.

evidence.source: Amazon Q2 2026 results release (aboutamazon.com official release copy, 2026-07-30)

evidence.claim: AWS AI business and chips business each exceeded $25B annualized run rate, growing triple digits; Trainium commitments from Anthropic and OpenAI (multi-year, multi-gigawatt)
evidence.source: Amazon Q2 2026 results release, CEO commentary
